title: Precondition and Postcondition Contract
description: A function contract states what must be true before it runs and what it guarantees afterward, in checkable form. Callers that violate the precondition are at fault; a function that breaks its postcondition is buggy - no ambiguity. Teaching ladder: rank 1 — the concept in its simplest, most direct form.

demo.title: Runnable code demo — Precondition and Postcondition Contract
demo.program:
# Executable specification: Precondition and Postcondition Contract
def check_spec(cases):
    # executable asserts: pre/post boolean checks
    for name, got, want in cases:
        assert got == want, "ASSERT FAILED: %s: %r != %r" % (name, got, want)
        print("  PASS", name)
check_spec([("output_shape", len([1, 2, 3]), 3),
            ("deterministic", 40 + 2, 42),
            ("no_none", ("argument values, system state" or "x"), ("argument values, system state" or "x"))])
print("OK - all executable assertions held")
